mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 4.0% over the past quarter predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as lower interest rates reduce discount rates on equity cash flows, boosting valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than a 60-day rolling average (t-test p > 0.05) during easing periods, or FEDFUNDS remains above 4.0% for the preceding 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% and upward momentum in monthly payrolls signals strengthening labor market conditions, driving investor confidence and positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% and PAYEMS increases by 5,000 in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite meeting the trigger condition, or UNRATE rises above 4.0% within the next 30 days after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 5% rise in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices over a month indicates overheating, prompting central banks to raise rates, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows 5% while INDPRO rises 2% in the next month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of high demand-supply growth, or central banks do not raise rates despite the inflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden crossing of the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as higher interest rates reduce the present value of future cash flows, dampening equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite the rate crossing above 4.5%, or the rate remains above 4.5% for less than a month post-trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in payrolls below historical averages for three consecutive months predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as weak labor demand signals economic slowdown and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during payrolls below trend, or payrolls rebound within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 4% increase in demand (GDPC1) and 1.5% rise in CPIAUCSL (inflation) over a month signals inflationary pressure, prompting central banks to hike rates, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases 4% while CPIAUCSL rises 1.5% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during inflationary periods, or central banks do not raise rates despite the inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a sustained monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 4.0% triggers positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as easing policies boost investor sentiment and equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 4.0% during late-cycle expansion
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during late-cycle periods when the trigger occurs, or the regime is not in late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 10% growth in demand (GDPC1) outpacing a 2% rise in supply (INDPRO) over a month indicates supply-demand imbalance, leading to inflationary pressures and central bank rate hikes that compress equity valuations, producing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds 10% growth while INDPRO rises by only 2% in the next month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during supply-demand imbalances, or central banks do not raise rates despite the imbalance.
